findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

The scoop used for ice in the bar area was observed with the handle in contact with the ice. This would require an employee to touch the ice with their bare hand to acquire the scoop and use it. Education was conducted with the PIC and they were instructed to review with staff to correct. Prevent all bare hand contact with ready to eat foods (ice in this case) in order to prevent possible contamination vectors.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

Someone was observed to pour and rinse out a cup in the hand sink in the kitchen area. The situation was discussed with the PIC to correct. Ensure that the hand washing sinks are not used for purposes other than hand washing at any time in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple “cleaned” and stored dishes are oberved soiled after storage. The items were all moved back to dish for re-cleaning to correct the violation. Ensure that all dishes are cleaned completely prior to storage.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) Food, Hot and Cold Holding. TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Numerous TCS foods in the walk in cooler are observed with internal temperatures between 46F-51F. These items were shown to the PIC and they items discarded during this inspection to correct the violation. Items discarded include: turkey, chili, prime rib, filets, ground beef (5 5lb logs), cooked rice, sliced cheddar cheese, sliced Swiss cheese, shredded cheddar cheese, milk, half n’ half, sour cream, cottage cheese, heavy cream, and alfredo sauce. Ensure that all TCS foods are maintained at 41F or below at all times.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The walk in cooler is not effectively maintaining TCS foods at safe cold holding limits during this inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to have maintenance service it prior to using it for TCS cold holding moving forward. A follow up is being scheduled for 10 days to verify compliance.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. 

The shelving in the walk-in cooler is beginning to peel, flake, and rust. Reseal/replace prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all surfaces do not pose a concern for contamination of foods stored in the coolers.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. 

The chest freezer in the kitchen is observed with the internal lid separating from itself and exposing insulation to the food contact items and food items inside. The PIC was notified and instructed to repair/replace prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. 

The facility has made significant progress in the mitigation of the roaches observed over the previous routine inspections. Major cleaning has taken place throughout the facility. Per the PIC, Bacon Pest has been to the facility three times since the previous routine inspection. The last visit was yesterday. Approximately 15 live roaches were observed throughout the facility during this inspection. Another follow up will be conducted in 30 days to verify compliance. Pests were primarily observed within the bar and service areas. See that items that are unnecessary to service are removed.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

The ice scoop in the bar ice bin is observed with the handle in contact with the ice. This would require an employee to touch the ice with their hands when grabbing the handle. Ice is considered a Ready-To-Eat food by the food code. The bartender was shown and moved the ice scoop to correct. Ensure that the RTE foods are protected from contamination at all times.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

Pink mold is observed on the deflector shield in the ice machine used by staff. An employee was shown and washed the surface to correct the immediate violation. Regular cleaning should be taking place for this item to ensure that all Ready-To-Eat foods are protected from contamination at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(D) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sani bucket in the server area is observed with a concentration of approximately 10 ppm CL. A minimum of 50 ppm is required for CL solutions. The server was shown and remade the bucket to correct the violation. Ensure that all sanitizers are at correct concentration in the facility at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The soda gun closest to the kitchen door is observed with mold growth inside of the nozzle. The server/bartender was shown and washed (wash/rinse/sanitize) during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned often enough to ensure that they do not grow pathogenic organisms.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13(B) Observed a container of chili to be thawing in the microwave. Microwave was not running and chili was sitting at room temperature within the device. The chili was still chilled, but not frozen. Educated on thawing during the inspection. Operator removed the chili from the microwave and began to reheat in a pan on the stovetop. 

Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.111 Observed the facility to be on the verge of a roach infestation. There are pests observed throughout the facility in various life stages. There are cleaning and maintenance of the facility is supporting the proliferation of these pests. There is cleaning and repair work to be completed (see violation # 16,47, 49, 55) in-order to insure pests are controlled. The facility has grease, dust, food, and water standing in places throughout the bar and kitchen. Pests are observed primarily in the dish area, on the far side of the bar (around the electronics), and around the preparation cooler across from the cook line. It is imperative that proper maintenance and cleaning take place to insure the facility continues to safely operate. The facility will not be allowed to operate with pests within equipment. Facility should insure that equipment has backing removed to allow interior to be treated. The facility will be revisited in thirty days to allow for proper cleaning, maintenance, and treatment. 

(A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

The knife bucket in the server area is observed with dust and food debris in the bottom. The PIC was notified and instructed to clean the container and knives and maintain them clean moving forward. All food contact surfaces need to be stored so that they are maintained free of contamination prior to use.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.11(A) The shelving in the walk-in cooler is beginning to peel, flake, and rust. See #55 for additional walk-in cooler details. There are laminated signs on the wall of the cook line with roaches stuck within. Remove the signage from the walls. There is a particle board shelf in the dish room that is starting to bubble and warp. Replace the shelving.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 The following surfaces shall be maintained clean:  1) the shelving beneath the microwave across from the preparation cooler is coated with grease and dust; 2) the plumbing under the triple sink is soiled; 3) shelving holding plates and utensils to left of cook line. Clean the aforementioned areas.

(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13  There is an old container of waste water beneath the bar triple sink. There is also ponding water to the left of the bar triple sink. See that waste water is emptied daily and maintained clean. The water under the triple sink is old and should be immediately emptied. Water ponding around the triple sink in the dish area should be removed AND the area maintained so ponding water is not an issue. 

Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-201.16(A) The following surfaces need maintenance attention:
This inspection will be focused on only the dish machine room and the walk-in cooler.
1) the walk-in cooler has chipped paint and rotted wood throughout - wall trim is rotted and chipping, the ceiling has peeled paint and water damage, the walls have water damage and chipped paint. Operator is aware of the concern and has placed Nudo board across one wall. The remaining walls need attention. 
2) The dish room has multiple holes, gaps, and peeling paint. There is a corner to the left of the dish machine that is not sealed, there are gaps in the paint, metal trim, and wall on the left side of the triple sink. There are gaps in the cove base/ wall board to floor. 

The walk-in cooler and the dish area are two action projects that need immediate attention in-order to prevent further disrepair. The walk-in cooler needs maintenance to prevent further damage and the dish area need maintenance in-order to curtail pest growth. 





Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 The entire facility has floors, walls, and ceiling that are coated with dust and grease. There is observed soil in nearly every corner. Dead roaches are observed in corners and floors throughout. The bar area has live roaches present around the electronic equipment (especially contained within the plastic cover of the receiver). Floor around the keg cooler are observed soiled with old bar debris. The entire store has an accumulation of grease, food, and dust present due to lack of cleaning. Clean the aforementioned surfaces. 

Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Multiple live roaches are observed in the bar area of the facility. The bartender and PIC were shown the live ones observed, killed during this inspection. Pest control has been to the facility and treated once since the previous inspection. Another treatment is scheduled for tomorrow. Another inspection will take place in two weeks to allow the treatments time to take effect and reduce the numbers.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani bucket in the server area is observed low on inspector test strips. The bucket was remade to correct the violation during this inspection. The worker consulted indicated that the bucket was made approximately 45 minutes prior to observation. Given the timeframe involved it is likely that the initial concentration when made needs to be stronger. Ensure that all sanitizers in the facility are correct at all times.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
3-602.11: (A) FOOD PACKAGED in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be properly labeled. (B) Regulatory requirements-(1) The common name of the FOOD. 

A container of white powder is on top of a freezer in the kitchen without label. The kitchen manager was consulted and indicated that it is sugar and labeled the container promptly to correct the violation. Ensure that all foods not in their original containers, especially ones not easily identifiable at a glance, have labels added.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Multiple live roaches are observed in the bar area of the facility. Numerous dead roaches are observed throughout the bar area. The bartender was shown and the live ones observed killed during this inspection. Thorough cleaning of the facility is needed to ensure that the current set of dead roaches has been removed and all new ones are found. Pest control also needs to be contacted and maintenance conducted prior to the follow up in 10 days. Due to the weekend and observed holiday the follow up date has been adjusted.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Two packages of soup are observed in the sinks next to the ice machines. PIC indicated that they were thawing. The soups were moved to the walk in cooler to correct.
